design_fidelity.notes: Matches (a2) adapters, (a4) voice keys and library layout, (a5) spend, D-20 (player-set ceiling default 0.50, bounds 0.05..20; AI_LIVE=1 so the unattended loop cannot spend) and D-21 (no digits in every prompt and screen; news cap 280, fixture over_length 309 chars). Text to OpenRouter first with both keys is preserved despite ailang#1536. -1: provider.ail:152-157 `estimate` is documented as the 'worst case' but is an approximation for input tokens (4 chars a token, chars4) while the admitted call is charged what the provider reports, so the ceiling can be overshot by one call's under-estimate; at the committed prices that is a fraction of a cent (about 300 prompt tokens at 0.30 $/Mtok), and output tokens and per-call prices are true bounds (token cap, maxOutputTokens, per_call), so it is a wording/robustness point, not a spend hole. Also noted (no deduction): live correctness depends on the launch flag `--ai gemini-2.5-flash-image` that AI.6 owns; the service cannot check which model std/ai is bound to.

deviation_verdicts.openrouter_over_std_net_not_std_ai_step: ACCEPTED, sound and secure; flagged for Mark at the style-frame stop as the executor asked. Sound: on v0.51.0 std/ai binds one provider per process (ailang#1536), so one process cannot both route text to OpenRouter through std/ai and make Gemini images; the alternative (two processes) costs AI.6 a second supervised child. Chat completions over std/net is a stable, documented API; the parser handles the error object, the empty choice list and the length finish. Secure: the key lives in one record, reaches one header, is never printed, never in hello/usage/index, and my runtime probe shows no leak when the runtime refuses an effect; transport errors are discarded, not echoed. Hosts are code constants; the runtime allowlist is AI.6/AI.9's launch flag and the design already lists openrouter.ai. Residual: the effectful OpenRouter and TTS halves have no automated exercise (see acceptance_criteria).
deviation_verdicts.adapters_split_adapters_ail_reply_ail: ACCEPTED. reply.ail (bodies, parsers, screen) is pure and runs on the strict VM in aiWireVm; adapters.ail is the only module with std/ai and std/net imports, which also keeps the stub loop's effect row at {IO, FS}. Better than the plan's single provider.ail.
deviation_verdicts.three_entries_and_ai_live: ACCEPTED. main keeps the AI.4 argument shape so AI.6's in-flight launch keeps working; session adds ceiling_usd (0.05..20, D-20); live is the only entry with Env/Net/AI and refuses before any call unless the provider's key is non-empty and AI_LIVE=1. The AI_LIVE requirement is defence in depth for D-20's 'the unattended loop never spends' ahead of AI.9's make-level guard; verified end to end with keys cleared and by two env mutants.
deviation_verdicts.stub_charges_routed_model_price: ACCEPTED. It is what lets usage.ndjson, per-provider totals and the budget refusal be exercised in make ai-stub without a key, and meta.provider 'stub' marks the price as simulated. Note for AI.9: the HUD must not present stub meta.usd as real spend.
deviation_verdicts.stub_goldens_rerecorded_and_budget_set: ACCEPTED. Re-recording was forced by D-21 (news 280), the cache_dir normalisation, the stub voice and the new usd field; the diff is confined to those. The budget set is the only automated proof of the ceiling at the file level (2 refusals, totals in usage.ndjson).
deviation_verdicts.deps_ai_first_in_ai_test_fetches_gemini_: ACCEPTED, verified on CI. Run 37053495105 (ubuntu-latest, clean runner, 18m27s, success): `cd ai && ailang lock` resolved sunholo/gemini_live@0.5.0 from the registry, then `git diff --exit-code -I generated_at ai/ailang.lock` passed, so the fetched content matched the committed content_hash (sha256:42f6598a...) and interface_hash. CI already needed the same registry access for sim/ (sunholo/relativity@0.5.1 fetched the same way at 19:20:53Z), so no new network requirement; the fetch is pinned by exact version in ailang.toml and by the lock hashes, and a registry drift fails the build rather than slipping in. Residual: if the registry is down, ai-test fails before any test runs, which is the same exposure sim/ has.

non_blocking_findings.issue: `failed` charges a failed live call's tokens (after = charge(l, j.hop.provider, n)), but nothing tests it: the mutant `after = l` survives package tests, ai-stub and ai-adapter. In live mode, repeated bad_output failures would then never move the ledger.
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Add to stub_test (or a new live_test case) a `failed` call with non-zero units: assert the ledger grows by cost(price, units), the usage line is emitted, and the error is last; and add it to ai-mutants.

non_blocking_findings.issue: The effectful OpenRouter (URL, Bearer header, body, retry) and TTS (x-goog-api-key, per-segment loop) halves run in no test; only their parsers do. AC9's 'both text adapters' is met only for Gemini.
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: A loopback fixture server under --net-allow-localhost (a Python harness is allowed by CLAUDE.md) serving the committed fixtures would exercise both without a key or a network; otherwise AI.10b's attended run must be written up as the only check.

non_blocking_findings.issue: nanoOf and field() round with +0.5 but no test distinguishes it from floor(); every committed price happens to round the same way (8.2 $/Mtok would give 8199 n$ without the +0.5).
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Add a price like 8.2 or 0.145 to spend_test's table and assert the n$ value.

non_blocking_findings.issue: The #1534 dirOf workaround (and the #1535 note at :9, the readFileBytes note at :77) says 'reported upstream' without the issue number; CLAUDE.md asks for the issue at the site.

non_blocking_findings.issue: The live launch block still shows `--entry main ... --provider gemini`, `--ai <text model>` and only generativelanguage.googleapis.com; AI.5 requires `--entry live`, `--ai gemini-2.5-flash-image`, AI_LIVE=1 and openrouter.ai in the allowlist (as the amendment table and as-built paragraph say).
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Update the block when AI.6 builds the launch, or mark it superseded now.

non_blocking_findings.issue: `estimate` is called the worst case, but input tokens are approximated (chars4), so a live call can be charged more than admitted and the ceiling overshot by that margin (fractions of a cent at the committed prices).
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Either say 'estimate' in the comment and design doc, or over-estimate input tokens (e.g. 2 chars a token) so the admitted figure is a bound.

non_blocking_findings.issue: anyDigit is tested with '42' only; dropping any one digit survives. Non-ASCII digits are not screened (the sim's ai_numeral is the judge).
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: One fixture per digit, or a '0123456789' case.

non_blocking_findings.issue: geminiImage: callImageBase64 returns a string, so a provider failure aborts the process (documented; ailang#1536 asks for a Result variant). A failed image is still charged per_call via `failed` (service.ail:157), which is right since the call was made.
non_blocking_findings.suggestion: None now; AI.6 supervision restarts the child.

non_blocking_findings.suggestion: Mark confirms or swaps at pause C; then re-record goldens.
